Question:
What changed between AC 43-9C and AC 43-9D?

Source: AC-43-9D, section 
AC 43-9D, Maintenance Records
Advisory Circular

Subject: Maintenance Records and FAA Form 8130-3 Return to Service

Date: 9/22/25

AC No: 43-9D

Initiated by: AFS-300 Change:

1 PURPOSE OF THIS ADVISORY CIRCULAR (AC). This AC provides information relevant to the public for the maintenance recordkeeping and record-making requirements of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) parts 43 and 91. This AC provides one means, but not the only means, of ensuring that the contemplated maintenance, alterations, or continue-in-service condition is in compliance with applicable regulations and existing policy.

Note 1: The information in this AC, with the exception of that information related to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Form 8130-3, Authorized Release Certificate, Airworthiness Approval Tag, does not apply to air carrier maintenance programs under 14 CFR §§ 121.367 and 135.425.

Note 2: This is a guidance document. Its content is not legally binding in its own right and will not be relied upon by the Department as a separate basis for affirmative enforcement action or other administrative penalty. Conformity with the guidance document is voluntary only. Nonconformity will not affect rights and obligations under existing statutes and regulations.

FAA Form 8130-3. The FAA has transferred the information regarding FAA Form 8130-3 from FAA Order 8130.21, Completion of FAA Form 8130-3 Under Part 21, into this AC. Furthermore, the FAA will incorporate the same information into FAA Order 8900.1, Flight Standards Information Management System, which is a comprehensive aviation safety inspector's (ASI) guide. The details moved to this AC and Order 8900.1 outline the instructions for FAA Form 8130-3 and the Airworthiness Approval Tag for approving return to service under 14 CFR part 43 of the regulations.

2 AUDIENCE. The audience of this AC is persons authorized by 14 CFR § 43.7(b)-(e) to approve aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, or alteration and FAA personnel tasked with the review and oversight of said entities.

3 WHERE YOU CAN FIND THIS AC. You can find this AC on the FAA's website at https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/advisory_circulars and the Dynamic Regulatory System (DRS) at https://drs.faa.gov.

4 WHAT THIS AC CANCELS. AC 43-9C, Maintenance Records, dated June 8, 1998, is canceled.

5 RELATED REGULATIONS. Title 14 CFR parts 1, 43, 65, 91, and 145.

Source: PROC-R7, section 
Procedures manual, revision 7 (excerpt)
Anfa Aero Services: procedures manual, revision 7 (excerpt)

| Revision | Date | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 2026-06-01 | Section 3.2 extended to every Cessna 172R and 172S; section 3.3 added. |
| 6 | 2025-09-29 | Section 2.4 and section 7 refer to AC 43-9D, which replaced AC 43-9C. |
| 5 | 2024-01-15 | Section 4.2: torque wrench calibration every 12 months instead of 24. |

Source: AC-43-9C, section 
AC 43-9C, Maintenance Records (cancelled 22 September 2025)
Advisory Circular

Subjet: MAINTENANCE RECORDS

Date:

6/8/98

AC No: 43-9C

Initiated by: AFS-340

Change:

PURPOSE. This advisory circular (AC) describes methods, procedures and practices that have. been determined to be acceptable means of showing compliance with the general aviation maintenance record making and record keeping requirements of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) parts 43 and 91. This material is not mandatory, nor is it regulatory and acknowledges that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will consider other methods that may be presented. It is issued for guidance purposes and outlines several methods of compliance with the regulations.

NOTE: The information in this AC does not apply to air carrier maintenance records made and retained in accordance with 14 CFR part 121.

CANCELLATION. AC 43-9B, Maintenance Records, dated January 9, 1984, is canceled.

RELATED REGULATIONS. 14 CFR parts 1, 43, 91, and 145.

DISCUSSION. The Code of Federal Regulations state that a U.S. standard airworthiness certificate is effective until it is surrendered, suspended, revoked, or a tèrmination date is otherwise established by the Administrator. In addition to those terms, a U.S. standard airworthiness certificate is effective only as long as the maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations are performed in accordance with parts 43 and 91, and the aircraft are registered in the United States. These terms and conditions are further restated, in block 6, on the front of FAA Form 8100-2, Standard Airworthiness Certificate. Qualified persons, who perform the maintenance, preventive maintenance and alterations, shall make a record entry of this accomnplishment, thus maintaining the validity of the certificate of airworthiness. Adequate aircraft records provide tangible evidence that the aircraft complies with the appropriate airworthiness requirements. In accordance with the terms and conditions listed in block 6 of the Standard Airworthiness Certificate, insufficient or non-existent aircraft records may render that standard airworthiness certificate invalid.

message.content:
Based on the supplied passages, the following changes were made from AC 43-9C to AC 43-9D:

1.  **Inclusion of FAA Form 8130-3 content**: AC 43-9D incorporates information regarding **FAA Form 8130-3 (Authorized Release Certificate, Airworthiness Approval Tag)** that was previously contained in FAA Order 8130.21. AC 43-9C does not mention this form. The new AC also states this information will be incorporated into FAA Order 8900.1. (Source: AC-43-9D, section 1)

2.  **Expanded Related Regulations**: AC 43-9D adds **14 CFR Part 65** to the list of related regulations (Parts 1, 43, 65, 91, and 145). AC 43-9C listed only Parts 1, 43, 91, and 145. (Source: AC-43-9D, section 5; AC-43-9C, RELATED REGULATIONS)

3.  **Explicit Audience Definition**: AC 43-9D adds a specific **AUDIENCE** section (Section 2) identifying the audience as persons authorized by 14 CFR § 43.7(b)-(e) to approve articles for return to service and FAA personnel. AC 43-9C does not have a distinct audience section. (Source: AC-43-9D, section 2)

4.  **Updated Applicability Notes**:
    *   AC 43-9D **Note 1** limits the non-applicability to air carrier programs under **14 CFR §§ 121.367 and 135.425** (specifically excluding FAA Form 8130-3 info from this exception).
    *   AC 43-9C **NOTE** broadly stated the information does not apply to air carrier maintenance records under **14 CFR Part 121**.
    *   AC 43-9D adds **Note 2**, explicitly stating the document is guidance only, not legally binding, and conformity is voluntary. AC 43-9C stated the material was "not mandatory, nor is it regulatory" within the PURPOSE section. (Source: AC-43-9D, section 1 Notes; AC-43-9C, PURPOSE and NOTE)

5.  **Structural and Administrative Updates**:
    *   AC 43-9D is organized into numbered sections (1-5), including a "WHERE YOU CAN FIND THIS AC" section with URLs.
    *   AC 43-9D cancels AC 43-9C (dated June 8, 1998). AC 43-9C cancelled AC 43-9B (dated January 9, 1984).
    *   Initiating office changed from **AFS-340** (AC 43-9C) to **AFS-300** (AC 43-9D). (Source: AC-43-9D, sections 1, 3, 4; AC-43-9C, CANCELLATION, Initiated by)

**Source Identification:**
*   **AC 43-9D** (Source: AC-43-9D, section)
*   **AC 43-9C** (Source: AC-43-9C, section)
